gen-gf-paprika-gf-savate: Loud, scattered letters with a reed-pen thickening: that's Paprika, filling the line like capitals. Savate follows in a sturdy, rounded sans whose open curves keep a long paragraph easy going.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-sulphur-point: Unica One has a huge lowercase eye, with daylight showing inside every curve it draws at a single thickness. Sulphur Point's marker-like line gives it a sturdy partner.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-stack-sans-notch: Stack Sans Notch reads big-bodied and open, with rod-stock strokes you can follow right into each curve. Wallpoet, in contrast, rises high with paper showing through its lines, and that stencil-like gap is the quality that defines this pair.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code runs wire-thin and monoline, with generous space between each neighbor. Trench Slab sits above it with outsized lowercase, so a larger heading size would let that bulk stand clear of the sans.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands in letters like pins in a wide board. Trench Slab brings oversized lowercase against that compact, thick-curved plain sans, so the heading shouts while the text stays tightly packed.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-julius-sans-one: Trench Slab's lowercase is oversized and industrial, built for a heavy first impression. And Julius Sans One answers with a plain sans of wide gaps, near-capital lowercase and curves left open-ended.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-lexend-exa: Chunky slab up top, wide and level below. Trench Slab's outsized lowercase sits over Lexend Exa, a sans-serif with one constant stroke width, big x-height and stubby ascenders.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-lexend-giga: Industrial weight leads here, with Trench Slab's outsized lowercase giving every heading a stocky, modern stance. Lexend Giga follows in flat single-weight lines, its generous tracking letting words breathe.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-lexend-mega: Stocky slab meets one-nib simplicity. Trench Slab's oversized lowercase sits above Lexend Mega, a sans-serif whose body height nearly matches its capitals, and that approachable evenness is the pairing's best asset.
gen-fs-trench-slab-gf-lexend-peta: Heavy slab letters over a wide, friendly sans-serif, with Trench Slab's outsized lowercase meeting Lexend Peta's bent-paperclip strokes and generous x-height. They fit snugly, one stocky, one open.
